day: # The Revised Common Lectionary (Consultation on Common Texts, 1992): the
# Sundays and festivals of Years A, B and C, as given by the Vanderbilt
# 2026, the three years 2025-26, 2026-27 and 2027-28, with the undated Sundays
# from its lists of texts).  Year A begins with Advent 2025.
# Shared by the calendars that keep the RCL: a tradition.csv names it with
# `readings,rcl` (see docs/traditions.md).  Every day is a date rule, so the
# file reads the same whatever the folder calls its days:
#   the Sundays after the Epiphany are counted from the Baptism (the Sunday
#   after 6 January) and give way to the Transfiguration, the last Sunday
#   before Lent; Propers 3-28 are the Sundays between their dates after
#   Christ the King (Proper 29) is the Sunday before Advent.
# After Pentecost the RCL has two series of Old Testament readings and
# psalms: semicontinuous (kinds ot_s, psalm_s) and complementary (ot_c
# psalm_c); the Episcopal Church calls them Track 1 and Track 2.
# The Easter Vigil is listed on Holy Saturday, the evening it begins.
